transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, they sent me here from work. Um, I was at the station—I'm an EMT—and I kept moving the airway bags into this specific pattern. I just knew it was the right way they needed to be arranged. I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud while I was doing it, too. 

My lieutenant came over and told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't do it. I couldn't. It just felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. So... they made me come here.
At the time, did you believe arranging the bags that way was truly necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, I did believe that. I had to do it because... well, I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. They've been going into the system and changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe. Whenever they pull me in, they tell me it's just routine paperwork, but I know what they're actually doing. So I had to make sure the bags were right.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or especially energized lately?

No, I haven't felt like that. I'm not... euphoric or bouncing off the walls or anything. My energy levels are just normal. I was just really focused on getting the bags right, that's all. I haven't felt unusually high or energized.
Do you believe it is definitely true that the supervisors are watching you through the cameras and changing your notes?

Yeah, I do. Like I was just saying... I know it for a fact. It's not a guess. The injury review guys and the supervisors are definitely watching the camera feeds. 

I've seen my triage notes after they've been changed in the system. They always try to play it off when they pull me in, telling me it's just routine paperwork or standard audits, but... I know what they're actually doing. They're altering the records to make me look like an unsafe provider. So, yes, it's definitely true.
Do you think there is any chance that arranging the bags in that exact pattern was not actually necessary?

No, I don't think there's any chance I was wrong about that. I know it sounds... I don't know, maybe it sounds strange to you, but I had to do it. If I didn't arrange them exactly like that, something bad would have happened. I know it for a fact. It was absolutely necessary.
How long have you been sure that your supervisors are watching you and changing your notes?

It's been about two months. Yeah, for the last two months I've known about the cameras and the paperwork stuff. And I guess that's how long the things I was doing at the station have been going on, too... the stuff that got everyone so alarmed. But yeah, about two months.
Have you been hearing voices that other people cannot hear?
No, I haven't heard anything like that. No voices or anything. It's just... well, just what I've seen them doing with the cameras and my notes. But no, no voices.
Have people been telling you lately that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

No, nobody has said anything like that to me. I mean, I think I speak pretty clearly. You know, you have to be able to communicate clearly when you're working on an ambulance, so... no, my speech is normal. No one has mentioned my thoughts being jumbled or anything.
During these past two months, have these beliefs and behaviors been present most days without a break for a month or more?

I... I'm not really sure if it's been every single day without a break. I mean, I know it's been going on for about two months, like I said, but I haven't exactly been keeping a calendar of it. I'm just working my shifts and dealing with it as it happens. So I couldn't tell you for sure if there was a full month straight where I noticed it every single day. I just know it's been happening.
Since these problems started, has your ability to do your job or handle your usual daily responsibilities gotten noticeably worse?

Yeah, it definitely has. I mean, I can't even work the ambulance anymore. They tried putting me on desk duty for a bit, just handling notes and equipment checks, but... well, I guess I got so unreliable with that, too, that they just took me off the schedule completely. And outside of work, it's... I don't really see my friends anymore. I've mostly just stopped keeping up with things around the house the way I used to. So, yeah, it's impacted a lot.
From the very first time these beliefs or unusual behaviors began, has it been six months yet?
Yeah, it's been longer than six months. This all started after I hurt my shoulder and ribs during an ambulance transfer... that was about eight months ago.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent delusional beliefs with bizarre/disorganized behavior and clear functional decline, with total illness duration over 6 months. He firmly believes supervisors are surveilling him and altering records, and he engaged in rigid, purposeless repetitive arranging behavior driven by delusional conviction. Mania and hallucinations were denied, and there is no evidence of formal thought disorder, but schizophrenia can be diagnosed when delusions and disorganized behavior are present with functional deterioration and sufficient duration.
